Comparing Cells
Common features: plasma membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes, genetic material
Prokaryotes vs. Eukaryotes:
Prokaryotes lack nucleus, membrane-bound organelles and internal membrane system; have a nucleoid where DNA is concentrated
Plant vs. Animal cells:
Plant cells have cell wall, central vacuole and plastids, not found in animal cells
explanation: This slide reviews cell comparisons. All cells share common features: a plasma membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes, and genetic material. Eukaryotes differ from prokaryotes because prokaryotes lack a nucleus, membrane-bound organelles, and an internal membrane system, instead concentrating their DNA in a region called the nucleoid. Within eukaryotes, plant cells contain three structures not found in animal cells: a cell wall, a central vacuole, and plastids.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature shared by ALL cells (prokaryotes and eukaryotes)?
questions.exp: The slide lists common features of all cells: plasma membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes, and genetic material.

questions.q: What structures are unique to plant cells and not found in animal cells?
opts: Cell wall, central vacuole, and plastids
questions.exp: Plant cells have a cell wall, central vacuole, and plastids, which are not found in animal cells.
